strategies.summary: With the prevailing bias, a down candle (or run of down candles) whose high is then broken is a bullish order block; enter when price returns to it. The block holds while no candle closes beyond 50% of its bodies.

timeframes.notes: No timeframes given in this video; fractal. Steps run on setup_tf, resolved at evaluation time (contract: timeframe ladder).

glossary.Mean threshold: 50% of the order block candle bodies, ignoring wicks; see custom_signals.mean_threshold_bodies.
glossary.Order block (bullish): A down candle (or run of consecutive down candles) coming off support whose high gets broken; see custom_signals.presenter_order_block.

custom_signals.name: presenter_order_block
custom_signals.plain_definition: A down candle (or run of consecutive down candles) coming off support whose high is subsequently broken; mirror for bearish.

custom_signals.name: mean_threshold_bodies
custom_signals.plain_definition: 50% of the bodies of the order block candle(s), ignoring the wicks.

custom_signals.name: ob_fvg_overlap_sensitivity
custom_signals.plain_definition: If the order block's wick overlaps a fair value gap, the wick extreme is the entry level; otherwise the body open is.
custom_signals.numeric_definition: (bullish_fvg[0].gap_high >= open[-1] AND bullish_fvg[0].gap_low <= high[-1]) * high[-1] + (1 - (bullish_fvg[0].gap_high >= open[-1] AND bullish_fvg[0].gap_low <= high[-1])) * open[-1]

sequence: Mark a down candle (or run of down candles) off support whose high is then broken: the bullish order block.
Buy when price returns to the block: at the wick top if the wick overlaps an FVG, otherwise at the body open.

invalidation.text: A candle closes beyond the mean threshold (50% of the order block bodies).

filters.text: The order block must align with the overall bias; not every down/up candle is an order block.
If the wick overlaps an FVG, the wick is sensitive; if not, the unmitigated orders are in the body.

entry_rule.text: Enter when price returns to the order block (at the wick if overlapping an FVG, otherwise the body).
entry_rule.quote: if it then returns to that order block we can possibly buy

presenter_claims.claim: order blocks alone could make you profitable

strategies.notes: The presenter's order block is looser than the engine's: it needs no FVG or BOS, only a broken high; the engine OB (order_block.*) is a stricter subset. His mean threshold is 50% of the bodies, not the engine's full-range midpoint (order_block.mean_threshold). The required bias is the presenter's directional bias (a liquidity sweep is given as one example of how it is set), not the engine structure bias; it is not computable from this video.

order_blocks.presenter_calls_it: one big order block (two consecutive down candles)

annotations_drawn_by_presenter.meaning: Highlights the top of the wick overlapping with an FVG as the sensitive entry level

setup_walkthrough.what_happens: Two consecutive down candles form, bouncing off a previous fair value gap acting as support.
The high of the consolidated order block is broken.
Price returns to mitigate the order block. Because the OB wick overlaps with an FVG, the top of the wick is the sensitive entry area.
The mean threshold (50% of the bodies) is strictly respected with no bodies closing below it, validating the block.

examples.presenter_commentary: The presenter emphasizes that an order block doesn't have to be a single candle; consecutive down candles act as one. He also introduces a key nuance: if the OB wick overlaps a fair value gap, the wick is the entry zone; if it doesn't, the unmitigated orders lie in the candle body.

may_differ.reason: Traidle defines mean threshold as the midpoint of the high-low range, but the presenter explicitly restricts it to 50% of the candle bodies, ignoring wicks.
If an FVG does not overlap the wick, the presenter uses the open of the body as the top of the sensitive zone, whereas Traidle uses the high of the candle.

structural_events.presenter_calls_it: sweep of the high / breakout traders trapped

signals_observed.bias_source: established after the buy-side liquidity sweep

setup_walkthrough.what_happens: Price sweeps above a previous high, hitting the buy stops of breakout traders, shifting the market bias to bearish.
An up candle forms coming off a small FVG (resistance), and its low is subsequently broken, confirming it as a bearish order block.
Price returns to the up candle. The bodies are used as the sensitive zone because there is no overlapping FVG with the wick. Mean threshold is respected.
The sequence repeats as a new up candle forms, its low is broken, price returns to mitigate it, respects the MT, and rejects away again.

examples.presenter_commentary: He explains the logic of liquidity sweeps trapping breakout traders to establish a bias. Once bearish, he demonstrates a sequence where multiple up candles act as valid bearish order blocks because they meet the criteria of bouncing off resistance, breaking their lows, and respecting the body mean threshold.

may_differ.reason: Same as previous example: relies on 50% of bodies, not the full candle range.

custom_signals_observed.name: rejection_block
custom_signals_observed.presenter_calls_it: rejection block / some kind of support

setup_walkthrough.what_happens: A series of consecutive down candles bounces off a rejection block. The high is broken, price returns, and respects the mean threshold.
A second bullish order block forms, using the first order block as support, and is also respected.
A subsequent order block forms, but experiences a deep downside rejection where price disrespects the mean threshold, causing the block to fail.

examples.presenter_commentary: The presenter highlights a sequence of successful bullish order blocks followed by one that fails (mean threshold is disrespected). He emphasizes this to show that no setup is perfect, trading is probabilistic, and the search for a 100% win-rate 'Holy Grail' is flawed.

may_differ.reason: Calculated strictly as 50% of the bodies, differing from standard range midpoint.
Traidle invalidates on a body close beyond the MT; the presenter notes the setup fails here but price still continues higher, meaning the structural trend didn't break even if the local OB failed.
